name: Bahia Principe Explore El Portillo

kids_club.evidence: The official site lists an included Kids Club for ages 4-12 (tour operators still call it Bahia Scouts) and a Teens Club for 13-17. Hours are not published anywhere we could find, and the few parent comments are mixed, from strong praise to one family finding it unwelcoming at midday.

water_play.evidence: A children's water park has slides and splash zones sized for kids 90-110 cm tall, which suits young children, with its own bar nearby; it sits alongside the resort's three pools.

beach.evidence: revised from 3: a very wide, soft-sand, calm beach that 2026 guests consistently praise as clean, with staff raking any seaweed. Sargassum is lighter here than in Punta Cana but not absent: a beach tracker showed moderate seaweed at the resort in early April 2026, so late-April risk is moderate.

rooms.evidence: revised from 4: standard rooms have two full beds or a king and take 2 adults + 1 child; junior suites add two doubles and a sofa bed. The resort's families page now confirms connecting options for groups of up to eight.

food.evidence: One buffet plus five à la carte restaurants (French, Brazilian steakhouse, Italian, Greek, seafood), with three à la carte dinners a week, booked on arrival or by app. 2026 guests rate the seafood and other à la carte meals highly and note a renovated, roomier buffet, but some find buffet dishes dry or inconsistent and report lunch queues.

transfer.evidence: PUJ is about 300 km away, a 4-4.5 hour drive. El Catey (AZS) is only 35-45 minutes away but has no US routes (only Canadian carriers and Air Caraïbes from Paris), and JetBlue's 2012 service to AZS is no longer listed.

condition.evidence: It reopened in December 2020 after a US$10M redesign that followed a fire. 2026 reviews are mixed: grounds, beach and staff are praised (about 4.3-4.5 out of 5 across roughly 9,000 Tripadvisor reviews), but several guests describe dated rooms with AC failures, leaks or musty smells, while some rooms have been renovated.

kids_club.name: Kids Club (historically Bahia Scouts)
kids_club.notes: The official site lists supervised activities; reviews mention crafts, games, pool play and an evening mini disco. Other Bahia Principe resorts reportedly close the club for a 12:30-14:30 lunch pickup, not confirmed here. Babysitting costs extra.

pros: A kids' water park with slides sized for a child about 90-110 cm tall
Rooms with two full beds, junior suites with two doubles plus a sofa bed, and connecting options
A wide, calm, raked beach that 2026 guests rate highly, with less seaweed than Punta Cana
Seafood, Greek, Italian and French à la carte choices, so the steakhouse is easy to skip
cons: No US nonstop to nearby AZS, so it means a 4+ hour drive from PUJ (SDQ is about 2.5-3 hours)
Only three à la carte dinners a week, all needing reservations
Kids' club hours are unpublished and parent reviews are mixed
Some rooms are dated, with 2026 reports of AC failures and leaks
verdict: The water park and beach suit young children, but with no US nonstop into El Catey the 4-hour transfer from PUJ rules it out for a short trip.
